lesson_scope: Forces acting at a point where the resultant is constrained to act along specific axes, lines, or directions; resolving forces to eliminate orthogonal components; setting up and solving simultaneous equations from directional and magnitude constraints; parameter optimization; and connecting constrained resultant forces to Newton's second law and kinematics.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 1: Horizontal cancellation to produce vertical resultant

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Horizontal cancellation to produce vertical resultant

hints: For the resultant force to act purely in the vertical direction, the total horizontal component must be zero ($R_x = 0$).
Resolve horizontally to form the equation $24 - F\cos 30^\circ = 0$, solve for $F$, and then evaluate the remaining vertical component $R_y = F\sin 30^\circ$.

walkthrough.text:
Set the total horizontal component equal to zero:
$$R_x = 24 - F\cos 30^\circ = 0$$
$$F\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 24 \implies F = \frac{48}{\sqrt{3}} = 16\sqrt{3} \approx 27.7\text{ N}$$

Calculate the magnitude of the resultant from the vertical component:
$$R = R_y = F\sin 30^\circ = (16\sqrt{3})\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 8\sqrt{3} \approx 13.9\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
When a resultant is constrained to act along the vertical axis, the net force along the horizontal axis must vanish completely:
- The $24\text{ N}$ force pulls directly rightwards along $+x$.
- The force $F$ pulls leftwards with horizontal component $F\cos 30^\circ$.
Equate these two opposing effects:
$$24 - F\cos 30^\circ = 0$$
$$F\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 24$$
$$F = \frac{48}{\sqrt{3}} = 16\sqrt{3} \approx 27.7\text{ N}$$

Because the horizontal forces cancel out to zero, the entire resultant force is just the vertical component:
- The $24\text{ N}$ force has no vertical effect ($0\text{ N}$ vertically).
- The force $F$ acts upward with component $F\sin 30^\circ$.
Evaluate the vertical pull:
$$R = R_y = F\sin 30^\circ = (16\sqrt{3})\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 8\sqrt{3} \approx 13.9\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets the total horizontal component to zero: $24 - F\cos 30^\circ = 0$.
Obtains $F = 16\sqrt{3} \approx 27.7\text{ N}$ and resultant magnitude $R = 8\sqrt{3} \approx 13.9\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 2: Vertical cancellation to produce horizontal resultant

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 2: Vertical cancellation to produce horizontal resultant

hints: A purely horizontal resultant means the net vertical force is zero ($R_y = 0$).
Set the upward force equal to the downward vertical component: $40 = 50\sin\alpha$, solve for $\alpha$, then calculate $R = 50\cos\alpha$.

walkthrough.text:
Set the net vertical component equal to zero:
$$R_y = 40 - 50\sin\alpha = 0$$
$$\sin\alpha = \frac{40}{50} = 0.8 \implies \alpha = \arcsin(0.8) \approx 53.13^\circ \approx 53.1^\circ$$

Determine the resultant magnitude from the horizontal component:
$$\cos\alpha = \sqrt{1 - 0.8^2} = 0.6$$
$$R = R_x = 50\cos\alpha = 50(0.6) = 30\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
When the resultant points horizontally along $+x$, the upward and downward vertical forces must balance out:
- Upward pull: $40\text{ N}$ along $+y$.
- Downward pull: $50\sin\alpha$ from the angled force below the horizontal.
Set up the vertical balance equation:
$$40 - 50\sin\alpha = 0$$
$$\sin\alpha = \frac{40}{50} = 0.8$$
$$\alpha = \arcsin(0.8) \approx 53.1^\circ$$

Since the vertical forces balance out completely, the horizontal component is the entire resultant force:
- The $40\text{ N}$ force is perpendicular to the $x$-axis, so it provides zero horizontal pull.
- The $50\text{ N}$ force provides the full horizontal push: $50\cos\alpha$.
Calculate the magnitude:
$$R = 50\cos(53.13^\circ) = 50(0.6) = 30\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets the total vertical component to zero: $40 - 50\sin\alpha = 0$.
Obtains $\alpha = 53.1^\circ$ (or $0.927\text{ rad}$) and resultant magnitude $R = 30\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 3: Three-force horizontal resultant constraint

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 3: Three-force horizontal resultant constraint

hints: The resultant acts along the $x$-axis, which means the sum of vertical components must be zero ($R_y = 0$).
Equate the upward component $20\sin 60^\circ$ to the downward force $P$, then sum the horizontal components $35 + 20\cos 60^\circ$ to get $R$.

walkthrough.text:
Set the vertical component of the resultant to zero:
$$R_y = 20\sin 60^\circ - P = 0$$
$$P = 20\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 10\sqrt{3} \approx 17.3\text{ N}$$

Sum the horizontal components to find the resultant magnitude:
$$R = R_x = 35 + 20\cos 60^\circ = 35 + 20(0.5) = 35 + 10 = 45\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Because the resultant is constrained to have zero vertical effect, the vertical forces must balance each other:
- Upward pull: $20\sin 60^\circ$ from the angled force.
- Downward pull: $P$ pulling directly down along $-y$.
Set up the vertical balance equation:
$$P = 20\sin 60^\circ = 20\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 10\sqrt{3} \approx 17.3\text{ N}$$

Next, find the net horizontal force which forms the complete resultant:
- The direct horizontal force: $35\text{ N}$.
- The horizontal component of the angled force: $20\cos 60^\circ = 10\text{ N}$.
Combine both positive contributions:
$$R = 35 + 20\cos 60^\circ = 35 + 10 = 45\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves vertically and sets the vertical component to zero: $20\sin 60^\circ - P = 0$.
Obtains $P = 10\sqrt{3} \approx 17.3\text{ N}$ and resultant magnitude $R = 45\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 4: Resultant constrained along 45 degree diagonal

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 4: Resultant constrained along 45 degree diagonal

hints: When a resultant is inclined at $45^\circ$ to the positive $x$-axis, its horizontal and vertical components are equal because $\tan 45^\circ = 1$.
Equate $R_y = R_x$ to find $Q = 18\text{ N}$, then use Pythagoras theorem $R = \sqrt{18^2 + Q^2}$ to find the magnitude.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the directional constraint $\tan 45^\circ = \frac{R_y}{R_x}$:
$$\tan 45^\circ = \frac{Q}{18} = 1 \implies Q = 18\text{ N}$$

Compute the resultant magnitude using Pythagoras theorem:
$$R = \sqrt{R_x^2 + R_y^2} = \sqrt{18^2 + 18^2} = \sqrt{324 + 324} = \sqrt{648} = 18\sqrt{2} \approx 25.5\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
A line at $45^\circ$ to the axes creates an isosceles right-angled vector triangle:
- Horizontal component: $R_x = 18\text{ N}$.
- Vertical component: $R_y = Q$.
Because $\tan 45^\circ = 1$, the vertical leg must match the horizontal leg:
$$\frac{Q}{18} = 1 \implies Q = 18\text{ N}$$

Now find the length of the resultant hypotenuse:
- Both legs of the triangle equal $18\text{ N}$.
Apply Pythagoras theorem:
$$R = \sqrt{18^2 + 18^2} = 18\sqrt{2} \approx 25.5\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies the direction condition $\tan 45^\circ = \frac{Q}{18} = 1$ to find $Q = 18\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 5: Unknown force from constrained horizontal resultant

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 5: Unknown force from constrained horizontal resultant

hints: Resolve vertically to cancel the vertical components: $25\sin\alpha - P\sin\beta = 0$.
Resolve horizontally to match the required resultant: $25\cos\alpha + P\cos\beta = 40$, then use $P = \sqrt{(P\cos\beta)^2 + (P\sin\beta)^2}$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve vertically and horizontally to isolate the components of force $P$:
$$R_y = 25\sin\alpha - P\sin\beta = 0 \implies P\sin\beta = 25(0.6) = 15\text{ N}$$
$$R_x = 25\cos\alpha + P\cos\beta = 40 \implies 25(0.8) + P\cos\beta = 40 \implies P\cos\beta = 40 - 20 = 20\text{ N}$$

Determine the magnitude $P$ using Pythagoras theorem:
$$P = \sqrt{(P\cos\beta)^2 + (P\sin\beta)^2} = \sqrt{20^2 + 15^2} = \sqrt{400 + 225} = \sqrt{625} = 25\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Break down the target forces along the axes:
- Vertical direction: The resultant has no vertical component ($R_y = 0$). The upward pull of the first force is $25 \times 0.6 = 15\text{ N}$. The downward pull of the second force must balance this exactly:
$$P\sin\beta = 15\text{ N}$$
- Horizontal direction: The total pull must equal $40\text{ N}$. The first force supplies $25 \times 0.8 = 20\text{ N}$. The second force must supply the remaining amount:
$$P\cos\beta = 40 - 20 = 20\text{ N}$$

Combine the two rectangular components of force $P$:
- Horizontal leg: $20\text{ N}$.
- Vertical leg: $15\text{ N}$.
Apply Pythagoras theorem to find the hypotenuse:
$$P = \sqrt{20^2 + 15^2} = \sqrt{400 + 225} = \sqrt{625} = 25\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets $R_y = 25(0.6) - P\sin\beta = 0$ to get $P\sin\beta = 15$ and $R_x = 25(0.8) + P\cos\beta = 40$ to get $P\cos\beta = 20$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 6: Perpendicular resultant vector closure

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 6: Perpendicular resultant vector closure

hints: Use vector components: $\mathbf{P} = (30, 0)$ and $\mathbf{R} = (0, 40)$, so $\mathbf{Q} = \mathbf{R} - \mathbf{P} = (-30, 40)$.
Calculate $|\mathbf{Q}| = \sqrt{(-30)^2 + 40^2}$ and find the angle with the negative $x$-axis using $\tan\theta = \frac{40}{30}$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the horizontal and vertical components of force $\mathbf{Q}$:
$$R_x = 30 + Q_x = 0 \implies Q_x = -30\text{ N}$$
$$R_y = 0 + Q_y = 40 \implies Q_y = 40\text{ N}$$

Calculate the magnitude and direction of $\mathbf{Q}$:
$$|\mathbf{Q}| = \sqrt{(-30)^2 + 40^2} = \sqrt{900 + 1600} = \sqrt{2500} = 50\text{ N}$$
$$\tan\theta = \frac{|Q_y|}{|Q_x|} = \frac{40}{30} \implies \theta = \arctan\left(\frac{4}{3}\right) \approx 53.13^\circ \approx 53.1^\circ$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Think of vector addition in terms of component cancellation:
- Force $\mathbf{P}$ pulls $30\text{ N}$ to the right.
- The resultant must have zero horizontal component and point $40\text{ N}$ upwards.
Force $\mathbf{Q}$ must cancel the entire $30\text{ N}$ rightward pull and provide the full $40\text{ N}$ upward pull:
$$Q_x = -30\text{ N}, \quad Q_y = 40\text{ N}$$

Now compute the magnitude and direction of vector $\mathbf{Q}$:
- Hypotenuse magnitude:
$$|\mathbf{Q}| = \sqrt{(-30)^2 + 40^2} = \sqrt{2500} = 50\text{ N}$$
- Angle above the negative $x$-axis:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{40}{30} \implies \theta = \arctan(1.3333) \approx 53.1^\circ$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets $Q_x = -30\text{ N}$ and $Q_y = 40\text{ N}$ using vector equation $\mathbf{P} + \mathbf{Q} = \mathbf{R}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Practice: Core Practice 1: Three forces with unknown magnitude and horizontal resultant constraint

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 1: Three forces with unknown magnitude and horizontal resultant constraint

hints: Resolve each of the three forces into horizontal and vertical components, taking care with signs in the third quadrant.
Sum the horizontal components: $28 + 30(0.8) - P\cos 30^\circ$, and sum the vertical components: $30(0.6) - P\sin 30^\circ$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve all three forces horizontally along the $x$-axis:
$$X = 28 + 30\cos\alpha - P\cos 30^\circ$$
Substitute $\cos\alpha = 0.8$ and $\cos 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$:
$$X = 28 + 30(0.8) - P\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 28 + 24 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}P = 52 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}P$$

Resolve all three forces vertically along the $y$-axis:
$$Y = 0 + 30\sin\alpha - P\sin 30^\circ$$
Substitute $\sin\alpha = 0.6$ and $\sin 30^\circ = 0.5$:
$$Y = 30(0.6) - 0.5P = 18 - 0.5P$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Resolve each force along the horizontal axis:
- The $28\text{ N}$ force pulls directly along $+x$, giving $+28\text{ N}$.
- The $30\text{ N}$ force pulls rightwards with component $30\cos\alpha = 30(0.8) = +24\text{ N}$.
- The force $P$ points below the negative $x$-axis, so its horizontal component pulls leftwards: $-P\cos 30^\circ = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}P$.
Combine the horizontal terms:
$$X = 28 + 24 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}P = 52 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}P$$

Resolve each force along the vertical axis:
- The $28\text{ N}$ force has no vertical effect ($0\text{ N}$).
- The $30\text{ N}$ force pulls upwards with component $30\sin\alpha = 30(0.6) = +18\text{ N}$.
- The force $P$ pulls downwards with component $-P\sin 30^\circ = -0.5P$.
Combine the vertical terms:
$$Y = 18 - 0.5P$$

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves forces along Cartesian axes in terms of $P$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 1: Three forces with unknown magnitude and horizontal resultant constraint

hints: A resultant acting entirely along the positive $x$-axis requires the total vertical component to be zero: $Y = 0$.
Set $18 - 0.5P = 0$ to find $P$, then substitute this value into the expression for $X$ from part (a).

walkthrough.text:
Apply the condition that the resultant has zero vertical component:
$$Y = 18 - 0.5P = 0$$
$$0.5P = 18 \implies P = 36\text{ N}$$

Substitute $P = 36\text{ N}$ into the horizontal component expression:
$$R = X = 52 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}(36) = 52 - 18\sqrt{3}$$
$$R \approx 52 - 31.1769 = 20.8231 \approx 20.8\text{ N}$$
Thus, the resultant force has magnitude $20.8\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Since the resultant is constrained to act along the positive $x$-axis, there can be no net upward or downward force:
- Upward pull: $18\text{ N}$.
- Downward pull: $0.5P$.
Set the vertical sum equal to zero and solve for $P$:
$$18 - 0.5P = 0$$
$$0.5P = 18$$
$$P = \frac{18}{0.5} = 36\text{ N}$$

With the vertical components in complete balance, the horizontal component forms the entire resultant:
- Substitute $P = 36\text{ N}$ into the horizontal equation from part (a):
$$R = 52 - 18\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$
Evaluate the arithmetic to 3 significant figures:
$$18\sqrt{3} \approx 31.1769$$
$$R = 52 - 31.1769 = 20.8231 \approx 20.8\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Evaluates $X = 52 - 18\sqrt{3} \approx 20.8\text{ N}$ to give resultant magnitude $R = 20.8\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Practice: Core Practice 2: Constant horizontal component with directional resultant constraint

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 2: Constant horizontal component with directional resultant constraint

hints: Resolve the $40\text{ N}$ force and the $50\text{ N}$ force horizontally along the $x$-axis.
Notice that force $F$ acts along the $y$-axis and has zero component in the $x$-direction.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve all forces horizontally:
$$X = 40 - 50\cos\theta$$
Substitute $\cos\theta = 0.6$:
$$X = 40 - 50(0.6) = 40 - 30 = 10\text{ N}$$

Deduce independence from $F$:
Since force $F$ acts entirely along the vertical $y$-axis, its component along the $x$-axis is zero:
$$F_x = F\cos 90^\circ = 0\text{ N} \implies X = 10\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Look at the horizontal forces acting on the particle:
- The $40\text{ N}$ force pulls directly rightwards: $+40\text{ N}$.
- The $50\text{ N}$ force acts in the second quadrant, pulling leftwards with component $50\cos\theta = 50(0.6) = 30\text{ N}$.
Calculate the net horizontal force:
$$X = 40 - 30 = 10\text{ N}$$

Explain why this value is independent of $F$:
- Force $F$ acts straight down along the negative $y$-axis.
- A purely vertical force has zero horizontal component:
$$F_x = 0\text{ N} \implies X = 10\text{ N}$$
Consequently, the horizontal component remains $10\text{ N}$ regardless of the magnitude of $F$.

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains $X = 10\text{ N}$ and notes that force $F$ has no horizontal component.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 2: Constant horizontal component with directional resultant constraint

hints: An angle of $45^\circ$ below the positive $x$-axis means the vertical component satisfies $Y = -X$.
With $X = 10\text{ N}$, resolve vertically to get $Y = 50(0.8) - F = 40 - F$, set $40 - F = -10$, and calculate $R = \sqrt{10^2 + (-10)^2}$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the directional condition for $45^\circ$ below the positive $x$-axis:
$$Y = 50\sin\theta - F = 50(0.8) - F = 40 - F$$
Since the direction is $45^\circ$ below the positive $x$-axis:
$$\frac{Y}{X} = \tan(-45^\circ) = -1 \implies Y = -X = -10\text{ N}$$
$$40 - F = -10 \implies F = 50\text{ N}$$

Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force:
$$R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2} = \sqrt{10^2 + (-10)^2} = \sqrt{100 + 100} = \sqrt{200} = 10\sqrt{2} \approx 14.1\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
An angle of $45^\circ$ below the positive horizontal axis means the downward vertical component must equal the rightward horizontal component in size:
- Rightward component: $X = 10\text{ N}$.
- Downward requirement: $Y = -10\text{ N}$.
Express the vertical component in terms of $F$:
$$Y = 50\sin\theta - F = 50(0.8) - F = 40 - F$$
Set $40 - F = -10$ and solve for $F$:
$$F = 40 - (-10) = 50\text{ N}$$

Now find the resultant force from these two equal perpendicular components:
- Horizontal leg: $10\text{ N}$.
- Vertical leg: $-10\text{ N}$.
Apply Pythagoras theorem:
$$R = \sqrt{10^2 + (-10)^2} = \sqrt{200} = 10\sqrt{2} \approx 14.1\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets $\frac{Y}{X} = \tan(-45^\circ) = -1$ with $Y = 40 - F$ and $X = 10$ to obtain $40 - F = -10$.
Obtains $F = 50\text{ N}$ and resultant magnitude $R = 10\sqrt{2} \approx 14.1\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve all four forces vertically, taking the upward direction as positive:
$$Y = 65\sin\alpha + 20 - 15 - P\sin\theta = 0$$

$$65\left(\frac{5}{13}\right) + 20 - 15 - 50\sin\theta = 0$$
$$25 + 5 - 50\sin\theta = 0 \implies 30 - 50\sin\theta = 0$$

Solve for $\sin\theta$ and calculate the angle $\theta$:
$$50\sin\theta = 30 \implies \sin\theta = \frac{30}{50} = 0.6$$
$$\theta = \arcsin(0.6) \approx 36.8699^\circ \approx 36.9^\circ$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify each vertical force component acting on the particle:
- Upward force: $65\sin\alpha = 65(5/13) = 25\text{ N}$.
- Upward force: $20\text{ N}$.
- Downward force: $15\text{ N}$.
- Downward component: $50\sin\theta$.
Calculate the net upward contribution of the fixed forces:
$$Y_{\text{fixed}} = 25 + 20 - 15 = 30\text{ N}$$

Since the resultant has zero vertical effect, set the net vertical sum to zero:
$$30 - 50\sin\theta = 0$$
$$50\sin\theta = 30$$
$$\sin\theta = 0.6$$
$$\theta = \arcsin(0.6) \approx 36.9^\circ$$

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves vertically and sets vertical sum to zero: $65\sin\alpha + 20 - 15 - 50\sin\theta = 0$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Practice: Core Practice 4: Simultaneous equations from horizontal and vertical resultant constraints

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 4: Simultaneous equations from horizontal and vertical resultant constraints

hints: Resolve horizontally: the component along the positive $x$-axis is $P\cos 30^\circ$, and along the negative $x$-axis is $Q\cos 60^\circ$. Set their difference equal to $20\text{ N}$.
Substitute the exact trigonometric values $\cos 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $\cos 60^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$, then multiply through by 2.
Resolve vertically: $P\sin 30^\circ + Q\sin 60^\circ - 30 = 0$, substitute $\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$ and $\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, and clear the fractions.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces horizontally along the $x$-axis:
$$R_x = P\cos 30^\circ - Q\cos 60^\circ = 20$$
Substitute $\cos 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $\cos 60^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$:
$$P\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) - Q\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 20$$
Multiply through by 2:
$$P\sqrt{3} - Q = 40$$

Resolve forces vertically along the $y$-axis:
$$R_y = P\sin 30^\circ + Q\sin 60^\circ - 30 = 0$$
Substitute $\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$ and $\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$:
$$\frac{1}{2}P + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}Q = 30$$
Multiply through by 2:
$$P + Q\sqrt{3} = 60$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set up the horizontal constraint where the resultant must equal $20\text{ N}$ rightwards:
- Force $P$ pulls rightwards: $+P\cos 30^\circ = +\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}P$.
- Force $Q$ pulls leftwards: $-Q\cos 60^\circ = -\frac{1}{2}Q$.
Equate this net horizontal force to $20\text{ N}$:
$$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}P - \frac{1}{2}Q = 20$$
Multiply the entire equation by 2 to clear fractions:
$$P\sqrt{3} - Q = 40$$

Set up the vertical constraint where the resultant must have zero vertical effect:
- Force $P$ pulls upwards: $+P\sin 30^\circ = +\frac{1}{2}P$.
- Force $Q$ pulls upwards: $+Q\sin 60^\circ = +\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}Q$.
- The third force pulls straight downwards: $-30\text{ N}$.
Set the vertical sum to zero:
$$\frac{1}{2}P + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}Q - 30 = 0$$
Multiply by 2 to obtain the second linear equation:
$$P + Q\sqrt{3} = 60$$

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves horizontally and equates to 20: $P\cos 30^\circ - Q\cos 60^\circ = 20$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 4: Simultaneous equations from horizontal and vertical resultant constraints

hints: From equation (1), express $Q$ in terms of $P$: $Q = P\sqrt{3} - 40$.
Substitute this expression for $Q$ into equation (2): $P + (P\sqrt{3} - 40)\sqrt{3} = 60$.
Expand and collect like terms: $P + 3P - 40\sqrt{3} = 60 \implies 4P = 60 + 40\sqrt{3}$, solve for $P$, and then substitute back to find $Q$.

walkthrough.text:
Rearrange the first equation to express $Q$ in terms of $P$:
$$Q = P\sqrt{3} - 40$$
Substitute into the second equation $P + Q\sqrt{3} = 60$:
$$P + (P\sqrt{3} - 40)\sqrt{3} = 60$$
$$P + 3P - 40\sqrt{3} = 60$$
$$4P = 60 + 40\sqrt{3} \implies P = 15 + 10\sqrt{3} \approx 32.3205 \approx 32.3\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Use the substitution method to eliminate variable $Q$:
- From equation (1): $Q = P\sqrt{3} - 40$.
- Replace $Q$ in equation (2):
$$P + (P\sqrt{3} - 40)\sqrt{3} = 60$$
Expand the term with $\sqrt{3}$:
$$P + 3P - 40\sqrt{3} = 60$$
$$4P = 60 + 40\sqrt{3}$$
Divide by 4 to find $P$:
$$P = 15 + 10\sqrt{3} \approx 32.3\text{ N}$$

hints: State the horizontal constraint: because the resultant points purely in the positive $y$-direction, the net horizontal component is zero ($R_x = 0$).
Resolve horizontally: $48 - P\cos\alpha = 0 \implies P\cos\alpha = 48$.
State the vertical constraint: the net vertical component must equal the resultant magnitude ($R_y = 35\text{ N}$), giving $49 - P\sin\alpha = 35 \implies P\sin\alpha = 14$.
Divide the two component equations to find $\tan\alpha = \frac{14}{48} = \frac{7}{24}$, and use Pythagoras $P = \sqrt{48^2 + 14^2}$ to calculate $P$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve horizontally to apply the condition $R_x = 0$:
$$R_x = 48 - P\cos\alpha = 0 \implies P\cos\alpha = 48$$

Resolve vertically to apply the condition $R_y = 35\text{ N}$:
$$R_y = 49 - P\sin\alpha = 35 \implies P\sin\alpha = 49 - 35 = 14$$

Determine the angle $\alpha$ by dividing the vertical and horizontal components:
$$\tan\alpha = \frac{P\sin\alpha}{P\cos\alpha} = \frac{14}{48} = \frac{7}{24} \approx 0.291667$$
$$\alpha = \arctan\left(\frac{7}{24}\right) \approx 16.2602^\circ \approx 16.3^\circ$$

Calculate the magnitude $P$ using Pythagoras theorem:
$$P = \sqrt{(P\cos\alpha)^2 + (P\sin\alpha)^2} = \sqrt{48^2 + 14^2} = \sqrt{2304 + 196} = \sqrt{2500} = 50\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Examine the horizontal forces acting on the particle:
- Force $\mathbf{F}_1$ pulls rightwards: $+48\text{ N}$.
- Force $\mathbf{F}_3$ pulls leftwards into the third quadrant: $-P\cos\alpha$.
Because the resultant has no horizontal motion or effect, these two must balance:
$$48 - P\cos\alpha = 0$$
$$P\cos\alpha = 48$$

Examine the vertical forces acting on the particle:
- Force $\mathbf{F}_2$ pulls upwards: $+49\text{ N}$.
- Force $\mathbf{F}_3$ pulls downwards: $-P\sin\alpha$.
The net upward force must equal the given resultant magnitude of $35\text{ N}$:
$$49 - P\sin\alpha = 35$$
$$P\sin\alpha = 14$$

Divide the vertical component by the horizontal component to eliminate $P$ and isolate the direction:
$$\tan\alpha = \frac{P\sin\alpha}{P\cos\alpha} = \frac{14}{48} = \frac{7}{24}$$
$$\alpha = \arctan(0.291667) \approx 16.3^\circ$$

Find the magnitude $P$ using the Pythagorean identity:
$$P = \sqrt{48^2 + 14^2} = \sqrt{2304 + 196} = \sqrt{2500} = 50\text{ N}$$
Both parameters are now determined: $P = 50\text{ N}$ and $\alpha = 16.3^\circ$.

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves vertically and sets $R_y = 35$: $49 - P\sin\alpha = 35 \implies P\sin\alpha = 14$.
Solves to obtain $P = 50\text{ N}$ and $\alpha = \arctan(14/48) \approx 16.3^\circ$ (or $0.284\text{ rad}$).

hints: A resultant perpendicular to the $x$-axis has zero horizontal component ($X = 0$).
Sum the horizontal components: $60 + P\cos\theta = 0$, which immediately gives $P\cos\theta = -60$.
Remember that $P$ is a magnitude, so $P \geqslant 0$. From $P = \frac{60}{|\cos\theta|}$, $P$ is minimized when $|\cos\theta|$ is maximized.
Since the maximum possible value of $|\cos\theta|$ is 1, the minimum value is $P = 60\text{ N}$, achieved when $\cos\theta = -1 \implies \theta = 180^\circ$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the perpendicularity constraint to the horizontal axis:
Since the resultant is perpendicular to the $60\text{ N}$ force (which acts along the $x$-axis), the net horizontal component is zero:
$$X = 60 + P\cos\theta = 0 \implies P\cos\theta = -60$$

Determine the minimum possible magnitude of $P$:
Since $P > 0$ and $-1 \leqslant \cos\theta \leqslant 1$:
$$P = \frac{-60}{\cos\theta} = \frac{60}{|\cos\theta|}$$
Because $|\cos\theta| \leqslant 1$, the minimum value of $P$ occurs when $|\cos\theta| = 1$:
$$P_{\min} = \frac{60}{1} = 60\text{ N}$$

Find the corresponding angle $\theta$:
With $P = 60\text{ N}$:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{-60}{60} = -1 \implies \theta = 180^\circ$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Notice the directional constraint:
- The $60\text{ N}$ force pulls directly along $+x$.
- A resultant perpendicular to $+x$ must point purely along the vertical $y$-axis.
- This means the horizontal components must cancel completely:
$$60 + P\cos\theta = 0$$
$$P\cos\theta = -60$$

Find the smallest force $P$ capable of cancelling this $60\text{ N}$ pull:
- Any angle other than directly opposite will waste part of $P$ on vertical pulling.
- To cancel $60\text{ N}$ horizontally with the least effort, $P$ must pull entirely to the left:
$$P = \frac{60}{|\cos\theta|} \geqslant 60\text{ N}$$
Thus, the minimum magnitude is:
$$P_{\min} = 60\text{ N}$$

State the direction of this minimum force:
- Pulling directly leftwards corresponds to an angle of:
$$\theta = 180^\circ$$

hints: Express the components with $P = 75\text{ N}$: $X = 60 + 75\cos\theta$ and $Y = 45 + 75\sin\theta$.
Equate $Y = X$: $45 + 75\sin\theta = 60 + 75\cos\theta \implies 75(\sin\theta - \cos\theta) = 15$.
Divide by 75 to show $\sin\theta - \cos\theta = 0.2$.

Use the harmonic identity $\sin\theta - \cos\theta = \sqrt{2}\sin(\theta - 45^\circ)$, so $\sqrt{2}\sin(\theta - 45^\circ) = 0.2 \implies \sin(\theta - 45^\circ) = \frac{0.2}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.141421$.
Solve for the two angles: $\theta - 45^\circ = 8.13^\circ$ and $\theta - 45^\circ = 180^\circ - 8.13^\circ = 171.87^\circ$ to find both values of $\theta$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the condition $Y = X$ for the resultant acting along the line $y = x$:
$$X = 60 + 75\cos\theta$$
$$Y = 45 + 75\sin\theta$$
Equate $Y = X$:
$$45 + 75\sin\theta = 60 + 75\cos\theta$$
$$75\sin\theta - 75\cos\theta = 60 - 45 = 15$$
$$\sin\theta - \cos\theta = \frac{15}{75} = 0.2$$

Express $\sin\theta - \cos\theta$ in harmonic form $R_0\sin(\theta - \alpha)$:
$$R_0 = \sqrt{1^2 + (-1)^2} = \sqrt{2}$$
$$\sin\theta - \cos\theta = \sqrt{2}\sin(\theta - 45^\circ)$$
Set equal to $0.2$:
$$\sqrt{2}\sin(\theta - 45^\circ) = 0.2 \implies \sin(\theta - 45^\circ) = \frac{0.2}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.141421$$

Find the principal solution for $\theta$:
$$\theta - 45^\circ = \arcsin(0.141421) \approx 8.1301^\circ$$
$$\theta_1 = 45^\circ + 8.1301^\circ = 53.1301^\circ \approx 53.1^\circ$$

Find the second solution in the range $0^\circ \leqslant \theta \leqslant 360^\circ$:
$$\theta - 45^\circ = 180^\circ - 8.1301^\circ = 171.8699^\circ$$
$$\theta_2 = 45^\circ + 171.8699^\circ = 216.8699^\circ \approx 216.9^\circ$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Translate the geometric condition into an algebraic constraint:
- The resultant must point along the line $y = x$, meaning its vertical and horizontal components are equal: $Y = X$.
- Horizontal component: $X = 60 + 75\cos\theta$.
- Vertical component: $Y = 45 + 75\sin\theta$.
Equate them:
$$45 + 75\sin\theta = 60 + 75\cos\theta$$
Collect trigonometric terms on the left:
$$75(\sin\theta - \cos\theta) = 15$$
$$\sin\theta - \cos\theta = 0.2$$

Transform the combination of sine and cosine using the harmonic form:
- Form: $R_0\sin(\theta - 45^\circ)$ where $R_0 = \sqrt{1^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{2}$.
Rewrite the equation:
$$\sqrt{2}\sin(\theta - 45^\circ) = 0.2$$
$$\sin(\theta - 45^\circ) = \frac{0.2}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.141421$$

Calculate the first angle solution:
- The primary acute angle is:
$$\arcsin(0.141421) \approx 8.13^\circ$$
Add $45^\circ$ to both sides:
$$\theta_1 = 45^\circ + 8.13^\circ = 53.1^\circ$$

Calculate the second angle solution from the sine symmetry in the second quadrant:
- The second angle is $180^\circ - 8.13^\circ = 171.87^\circ$.
Add $45^\circ$ to both sides:
$$\theta_2 = 45^\circ + 171.87^\circ = 216.9^\circ$$
Both angles satisfy the directional constraint: $\theta = 53.1^\circ$ and $\theta = 216.9^\circ$.
